text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday.
- Zagreb citizens handed over to the police some 1,700 unregistered rifles and pistols worth 800,000 kuna up to January 7 deadline, set by the new law regulating arms posession.
- Opposition party leaders slam "the Memorandum", a new document listing future rights of the rebel Serbs in East Slavonia, for what they describe as allowing ethnic structure chances.
- Health inspectors fined 13 of 28 employers in capital Zagreb who failed to enforce the new smoking ban at work.
- Croatioa suffered 37 million kuna damage in 1996 due to floods, hail an earthquakes.
- Profitable enterpreneurs to suffer burden of the profit tax increase by 10 percent to 35 this year.
- Electricity consumption in Croatia rose by 5.9 percent last year. Government claims this confirms their estimates of 10 percent GDP growth in the same period.
- Asian concerns including Samsung, Hyundai, Daewoo and KIA show interest to invest in construction in Croatia.
- Slovenian side ordered a 200 million German marks worth repair job on the jointly-owned Krsko nuclear plant from Siemens-Framat.
- Ruling party said to be preparing constitutional changes to enable parliament to elect president of the republic.
- Kningips, in which the Austrian unit of Germany's Knauf recently purchased 42 percent, soon to restart production of gypsum. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
